title: Classification Drives Geographic Bias in Street Scene Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2412.11061v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Previous studies showed that image datasets lacking geographic diversity can lead to biased performance in models trained on them. While earlier work studied general-purpose image datasets (e.g., ImageNet) and simple tasks like image recognition, we investigated geo-biases in real-world driving datasets on a more complex task: instance segmentation. We examined if instance segmentation models trained on European driving scenes (Eurocentric models) are geo-biased. Consistent with previous work, we found that Eurocentric models were geo-biased. Interestingly, we found that geo-biases came from classification errors rather than localization errors, with classification errors alone contributing 10-90% of the geo-biases in segmentation and 19-88% of the geo-biases in detection. translated_title: 分类驱动街景分割中的地理偏差
translated_abstract: 以往的研究表明，缺乏地理多样性的图像数据集会导致在其上训练的模型产生有偏差的性能。虽然早期工作研究的是通用图像数据集（如ImageNet）和图像识别等简单任务，我们则在更复杂的任务——实例分割上，研究了真实世界驾驶数据集中的地理偏差。我们检验了在欧洲驾驶场景上训练的实例分割模型（欧洲中心模型）是否存在地理偏差。与以往工作一致，我们发现欧洲中心模型存在地理偏差。有趣的是，我们发现地理偏差来源于分类错误而非定位错误，仅分类错误就贡献了分割中10-90%的地理偏差以及检测中19-88%的地理偏差。这表明虽然分类存在地理偏差，但定位（包括检测和分割）在地理上是稳健的。我们的发现表明……
tldr: 该研究发现驾驶场景分割模型的地理偏差主要源于分类错误而非定位错误，分类错误单独贡献了分割中10-90%和检测中19-88%的地理偏差，说明定位能力在地理上是稳健的。
en_tdlr: Geo-biases in street scene segmentation stem from classification errors rather than localization errors, with classification alone contributing 10-90% of segmentation and 19-88% of detection geo-biases, indicating that localization is geographically robust.
